programs.description: 72-unit, 3-year professional doctorate preparing advanced practice nurses across five nurse practitioner specialization tracks. Hybrid delivery (synchronous and asynchronous online). Requires 1,000 clinical hours and current RN employment at time of application. Best-documented admission requirements of the 6 doctoral programs.
concentrations: Psychiatric-Mental Health Across the Life Span

advisor.name: Dr. Cleddhy Arellano
advisor.notes: Additional contacts: dnp@csulb.edu or (562) 985-4463. Mandatory pre-application information session must be attended before submitting application.

deadlines.notes: Cal State Apply is the sole application portal. PTCAS is NOT required for DNP (differs from DPT).

funding_signals.notes: No program-specific assistantships or fellowships documented on program pages. Clinical placement model makes traditional academic assistantships unlikely, though not explicitly ruled out. HRSA Nurse Corps scholarships and loan repayment programs exist nationally for advanced nursing students — external programs not CSULB-administered; eligibility requires direct verification.

admissions_fit.notes: Requires: BSN from accredited program (minimum 3.0 GPA), active unencumbered California RN license, college-level Statistics course, minimum 1 year clinical RN experience, current RN employment at time of application, three professional references, personal statement. Mandatory pre-application information session attendance. Interview required for selected applicants.

programs.source_notes: Concentrations, career outcomes, and admission requirements sourced from bsn-dnp-program page. Interest tags manually curated from concentration track names and clinical focus areas. academic_background_tags set to 'available' because BSN and active CA RN license are explicit admission requirements, directly confirming background. manual_review_required=true because interest_tags are manual_curated.

programs.description: Entry-level clinical doctoral program training physical therapists through 7 active research laboratories covering balance, biomechanics, electrophysiology, pathokinesiology, and spine research. CAPTE accredited. Prepares graduates for board specialty certification through ABPTS. Requires dual application via PTCAS and Cal State Apply.

advisor.name: Dr. Jeff Rodrigues
advisor.notes: Departmental inbox. No direct advisor phone listed in programs.json. For program questions, use CHHS-PT@csulb.edu.

deadlines.notes: Dual application required: (1) PTCAS application closes November 1. (2) Cal State Apply closes January 15. Both must be submitted. GRE required — PTCAS institution code 4389.

funding_signals.notes: No program-specific assistantships or fellowships documented. DPT is an entry-level clinical degree; traditional academic assistantships are uncommon in clinical PT programs. CDIP applicable for students targeting CSU faculty career in physical therapy education.

admissions_fit.notes: Entry-level program — no prior clinical license required. Prerequisite coursework (typically biology, chemistry, physics, anatomy, physiology, psychology) documented through PTCAS, not CSULB program pages. GRE required (PTCAS code 4389). For CSULB-specific admissions questions contact CHHS-PT@csulb.edu.

programs.description: Joint doctoral program with Claremont Graduate University (established 1987), integrating advanced engineering disciplines with computational mathematics. CSULB handles engineering coursework; CGU handles mathematics components. Only research-oriented doctoral program at CSULB. Accepts both fall and spring applicants. STEM-designated degree program.

advisor.name: Dr. Kerop Janoyan
advisor.notes: Associate Dean, College of Engineering. Office: ECS-617. Joint program — CGU faculty also involved in doctoral committee.

deadlines.notes: Only doctoral program at CSULB accepting spring admission — two complete admission cycles per year.

funding_signals.notes: Graduate Research Assistant positions exist within the College of Engineering (Civil Engineering and Transportation Engineering noted in departmental job postings). No formal RA program, stipend amounts, or application process documented on program pages. NSF Graduate Research Fellowships and NDSEG Fellowships are relevant external funding for STEM doctoral students — not CSULB-administered; contact Dr. Janoyan for internal funding opportunities.

admissions_fit.notes: GPA minimum, GRE requirement, and prerequisite coursework absent from all CSULB program pages. Joint PhD Program Handbook referenced on department page but not publicly accessible. Contact Dr. Kerop Janoyan at kerop.janoyan@csulb.edu or (562) 985-8032, Office ECS-617.
